subject:
Re: Redwood DPA / SCC module selection 




 follow-up from discovery call

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood / Acme discovery 

 DPA, SCC modules, SOC2

Hi Sarah / John —

Thanks again for the call this morning 

 appreciated the time and the clear questions on security and GDPR. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to procurement/legal: 

Summary from call:
- Acme is the Controller for customer data; Redwood will be the Processor.
- Key asks: DPA execution, SCC module selection for international transfers, SOC 2 Type II evidence, and initiation of the vendor security questionnaire.

What we’ll provide by EOD: 
1) Draft DPA (attached: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) — this is our standard DPA with the new SCC appendix.
2) SCC guidance doc (attached: SCC-Module-Choice.docx) — recommendation below.
3) SOC 2 status: Type II audit in progress; expected completion and report delivery by end of Oct 2026.
4) A link to our security questionnaire answers / artifacts in Drive (I’ll add the link once rishi confirms).

Recommendation on SCC modules (high level):
- Primary: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) between Acme (Controller) and Redwood (Processor). This covers the data flow from Acme to Redwood.
- If Redwood engages subprocessors (e.g., cloud infra providers) and there are onward transfers, Redwood will place Module 3 clauses with those subprocessors as Processor -> Subprocessor agreements. We’ll include the appropriate clauses in the SCC appendix so you don’t need separate templates for each subprocessor.

Action items / next steps: 
- Sarah: confirm that Acme will sign a Controller -> Processor DPA (Module 2) and whether you require the Module 3 text embedded/attached for subprocessors.
- John: please share any mandatory procurement redlines or your standard DPA template if you want us to review.
- Rishi (cc): can you confirm SOC 2 ETA and whether we should proactively provide the SOC 2 bridge letter in the meantime?

I’ve attached the DPA and the SCC guidance doc. If that looks okay I can send a DocuSign envelope for signature and loop in legal to take redlines. Happy to schedule a short follow-up next week (15–20 min) to finalize.

Best,

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah 


quick answers and adding Rishi (Legal) for the audit language: 

1) SCC modules: For the direct relationship between Acme (Controller) and Redwood (Processor) you will execute Module 2 (Controller -> Processor). That’s the standard pattern and is what our DPA’s SCC appendix references.
2) Subprocessors: We include Module 3 language for Redwood->subprocessor relationships in our Subprocessor Appendix. You do not need separate SCCs with each subprocessor — we pass down the appropriate clauses to our subprocessors (Module 3) and can provide evidence of that flow if required.

SOC 2 status (from Rishi):
Rishi here — Redwood is currently in the SOC 2 Type II audit period covering May 1–Aug 31, 2026. The control testing is complete and the auditor is finalizing reports. We expect the finalized SOC 2 Type II report to be available and shareable by Oct 31, 2026.

We can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter and our current SOC 2 Type I artifacts in the meantime for procurement review; happy to share those under an NDA if needed.

I’ve attached an SCC guidance doc that maps Module 2/3 to common customer scenarios. If you want, I can schedule a short session between your security team and Rishi to walk through specifics.

—
Marissa on behalf of Rishi
